ideas.name: braced long slide
ideas.description: The catalogue long_slide (sector_radius 50 mm, 103 mm opening, face 0 deg, tip +1 mm, 32 N) gives the geometry the wide objects need. It fails for two reasons. First, its 3x150 rods are cantilevered: at an 85-96 mm opening they are 94 mm out from the clamp, the rack lifts 2.2 mm off the gear (teeth skip past 0.5 mm), and each LM3UU carries 138 N vs 52.9 N rated. Second, the carriage has only two bushings. The braced version clamps the rods at both ends in a printed closed frame, which makes them simply supported and cuts deflection by more than 10x. It also uses four bushings spaced 30 mm apart on a longer carriage to share the moment, and a backing roller on an MR63 bearing behind the rack to hold it in mesh.
ideas.test: Add a long_slide variant to the simulator with rods supported at both ends (simply supported span), 4 bushings, and a rack backing roller. Then check rack lift (<0.5 mm) and per-bushing load at 85-96 mm openings, and run the pudding, sugar, mustard and tuna grasps.

ideas.name: flexure-mounted self-aligning moving pad
ideas.description: The moving pad is mounted on a printed TPU living hinge: a 1.5 mm web across the pad's mid-height that acts as a centring spring. Its rest angle is 28 deg, the current setting that keeps banana and the small objects. On a flat box side, the top corner presses first. That off-centre load rotates the pad about the flexure, up to about ±30 deg, until the face lies flat on the side, so the contact becomes horizontal and opposed instead of pushing 85 deg down on the top. This fixes the face tilt of the revolute jaw at every opening (+30 deg at 85 mm, more at 92-96 mm) without the wedge that breaks banana. Tip height is not the limit: with the fixed tip near the table, the moving tip at 90 mm is about +27 mm, which is below pudding's 38 mm top.
ideas.test: The simulator would need a pad body joined to the moving jaw by a hinge joint with stiffness (the flexure: about 0.05 N*m/rad, rest at 28 deg, limits ±30 deg). Then run pudding, sugar, mustard and tuna, plus banana and the round held objects.

ideas.name: link-driven variable-angle moving pad
ideas.description: The moving pad hangs on a pin at the jaw's fingertip, turning on two MR63 bearings. A short printed link (about 20 mm, two more pins) ties the pad's heel to a point on the gripper frame near the hinge axis, forming a small four-bar. As the jaw opens, the link turns the pad back relative to the jaw. The pad's tilt therefore grows from about 28 deg near closed to about 50 deg at 90 mm instead of staying fixed. Near closed, the fingertip dips only about -2 mm (the current banana-safe geometry). At 75-95 mm the face stays within about 10 deg of parallel and the fingertip stays within about +12 mm of the fixed one (better than b000's 45 deg, which already gained pudding, sugar and tuna). The fixed pad is unchanged: TPU 2 mm, reach 5 mm.
ideas.test: A pads variant in which the moving pad is a body jointed to the jaw at its fingertip, with its angle constrained by a link equation tied to the jaw angle (an equality constraint or coupled joint). Sweep the tilt schedule from 28 deg at closed to 50 deg at 1.0 rad, then rerun banana, dice and the four wide boxes.

ideas.name: convex rocker moving pad
ideas.description: A printed moving pad whose contact face is a circular arc in the jaw's swing plane, about 30 mm long and spanning tilts from 28° (top) to 48° (bottom), with a 2 mm TPU skin. As the hinge opens, the contact rolls down the arc, so some point always has a horizontal normal for jaw angles of about 0.49–0.95 rad (45 to roughly 90 mm). The fixed pad stays flat. It is mounted with the existing M2 screws, and reach stays 11 mm so the tip clears the fixed pad at the closed jaw.
ideas.test: A pads variant in design/fingers.py with a face_profile option ('flat' | 'arc'), taking arc_top_deg and arc_bottom_deg. Run the same interference check at −0.17..1.20 rad, then all 21 groups, with banana and the 85–96 mm boxes first.

ideas.name: split-reach pads (independent fixed and moving pad reach)
ideas.description: The same printed TPU-skinned pads (31 deg moving pad angle, 12 mm wide), with the reach parameter split into reach_fixed_mm and reach_moving_mm. The moving pad keeps its 17 mm extension, which offsets the hinge fingertip's rise at 85–96 mm openings. The fixed pad, whose face is a vertical plane and never rises, is shortened. This frees vertical clearance for tall upright objects without giving back the moving-tip margin that low wide boxes need.
ideas.test: Add a second reach parameter to design/fingers.py so the fixed and moving pads are generated at different lengths. Then run the 21 groups at moving 17 / fixed 11 and moving 17 / fixed 14, and report which pad carries the rim contact on potted_meat_can.

ideas.name: fixed-side cradle lip with close stop
ideas.description: Reprint the pads. The fixed pad gets a 3 mm inward hook along its bottom edge, angled up 10° so its upper surface acts as a ledge. The moving pad gets a 2 mm relief at its bottom inner corner so the hook has a pocket at the minimum opening. A small PLA stop tab screws to the jaw servo horn and meets the fixed jaw at 0.12 rad, so the pads never enter the −0.04 to 0.08 rad overlap that refused the catalogue lip. Wide lying objects that the tilted moving face pushes down (mustard) come to rest on the fixed-side ledge instead of sliding out under the fixed jaw.
ideas.test: The simulator would need a pads builder with lip_mm applied to the fixed pad only, a relief pocket on the moving pad, and a minimum servo angle set by the stop (q_min = 0.12 rad). Then run mustard_bottle plus all held groups, and pass the interference check over 0.12 to 1.20 rad.

proposals.edit: pads -> pads (groove_mm=0, lip_mm=0, pad_angle_deg=45, pad_tpu_mm=2, reach_mm=5, width_mm=12)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face. At wide openings the stock hinge swings the moving fingertip up: +22 mm at 85 mm (tuna, pudding) and +14 mm at 74-75 mm (sugar). The face is also 53 deg off parallel with its bottom swung out, so the jaw lands on the top edge pushing 55-84 deg down. Potted meat fails as squeezed_down_out: at 57 mm the face is 28-33 deg off and touches the top edge (+43 mm vs top +42), pushing 33 deg down against metal friction 0.35.
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel to the fixed face at one opening only. Tilting the moving pad back by pad_angle moves that opening wider and lowers the fingertip relative to the fixed one. With pad_angle 45 the brief gives: 85 mm opening at face +14 deg (was +53) and tip +14 mm (was +23); 55 mm at face -8 deg and tip -5 mm. A TPU skin raises friction from 0.45 to 0.9, so a residual tilt a holds when tan a < mu (tan 14 deg = 0.25).
proposals.hypothesis: For tuna (34 tall), System 1 can grasp deeper so the fixed tip sits about 4 mm above the table. The moving tip then lands about 18 mm up, below the top (34 mm), on a face only about 14 deg off parallel. For pudding (38 tall) and sugar (45 tall) it lands at about 22-26 mm, also below the top. Potted meat at 57 mm gets a nearly parallel face (about -7 deg), and the 0.9 friction carries 370 g easily (2*0.9*20 N = 36 N vs 3.6 N). Arm torque is fine: sugar needs 0.41 + 0.77 = 1.18 N*m vs a 1.62 stall. No cheaper move exists: System 1 already searched every grasp parameter, and the stock jaw's geometry fixes the tip rise. The pads cost $0, 18 machine minutes and items already on hand.
risks: dice / large_marker / wood_block_cube: at 17-35 mm the moving pad sits -21 deg or more with its tip about 10 mm below the fixed one, so it pushes small objects up and System 1 must raise the grasp to keep the moving tip off the table. TPU friction 0.9 is well above tan 21 deg = 0.38, so the push is held. Most at risk is dice (17 mm tall).
golf_ball / strawberry / plum / lemon (round): contacts no longer at the equator could push them up. TPU friction and System 1's depth tuning should absorb this.
apple / gelatin_box / banana (70-75 mm): the face goes from about +44 deg to about +5 deg there, which should help these; the max opening drops 99 -> 95 mm, still enough for them.

proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel to the fixed face at only one opening, and pad_angle sets that opening. This tests whether a midpoint keeps enough of the wide-object gain while staying close enough to 28 deg for banana. It costs nothing: a pad reprint of about 13 machine minutes. idea.name: flexure-mounted self-aligning moving pad
idea.description: The moving pad is mounted on a printed TPU living hinge: a 1.5 mm web across the pad's mid-height that acts as a centring spring. Its rest angle is 28 deg, the current setting that keeps banana and the small objects. On a flat box side, the top corner presses first. That off-centre load rotates the pad about the flexure, up to about ±30 deg, until the face lies flat on the side, so the contact becomes horizontal and opposed instead of pushing 85 deg down on the top. This fixes the face tilt of the revolute jaw at every opening (+30 deg at 85 mm, more at 92-96 mm) without the wedge that breaks banana. Tip height is not the limit: with the fixed tip near the table, the moving tip at 90 mm is about +27 mm, which is below pudding's 38 mm top.
idea.test: The simulator would need a pad body joined to the moving jaw by a hinge joint with stiffness (the flexure: about 0.05 N*m/rad, rest at 28 deg, limits ±30 deg). Then run pudding, sugar, mustard and tuna, plus banana and the round held objects.

idea.name: link-driven variable-angle moving pad
idea.description: The moving pad hangs on a pin at the jaw's fingertip, turning on two MR63 bearings. A short printed link (about 20 mm, two more pins) ties the pad's heel to a point on the gripper frame near the hinge axis, forming a small four-bar. As the jaw opens, the link turns the pad back relative to the jaw. The pad's tilt therefore grows from about 28 deg near closed to about 50 deg at 90 mm instead of staying fixed. Near closed, the fingertip dips only about -2 mm (the current banana-safe geometry). At 75-95 mm the face stays within about 10 deg of parallel and the fingertip stays within about +12 mm of the fixed one (better than b000's 45 deg, which already gained pudding, sugar and tuna). The fixed pad is unchanged: TPU 2 mm, reach 5 mm.
idea.test: A pads variant in which the moving pad is a body jointed to the jaw at its fingertip, with its angle constrained by a link equation tied to the jaw angle (an equality constraint or coupled joint). Sweep the tilt schedule from 28 deg at closed to 50 deg at 1.0 rad, then rerun banana, dice and the four wide boxes.

proposals.principle: Two contacts hold when their normals are horizontal and opposed. A convex (rocker) face, curved about an axis along the pad width, has some point with a horizontal normal at every jaw angle inside its arc. So the contact stays antipodal across a range of openings instead of one, and only the contact height shifts.
proposals.hypothesis: No catalogue part can do this. Pads are flat at a single angle. Parallelogram raises the tip 61 mm at 85 mm. A rocker pad whose arc runs from the 28° to the 48° tilt keeps today's behaviour at 17–55 mm, where the upper, 28° end of the arc touches. At 75–96 mm the lower, 45°+ end touches, about 14–25° better than now. Below about 70 mm the pad sits no further in than today's, so banana's start pose should not change.

idea.name: convex rocker moving pad
idea.description: A printed moving pad whose contact face is a circular arc in the jaw's swing plane, about 30 mm long and spanning tilts from 28° (top) to 48° (bottom), with a 2 mm TPU skin. As the hinge opens, the contact rolls down the arc, so some point always has a horizontal normal for jaw angles of about 0.49–0.95 rad (45 to roughly 90 mm). The fixed pad stays flat. It is mounted with the existing M2 screws, and reach stays 11 mm so the tip clears the fixed pad at the closed jaw.

I don't propose a catalogue swap, because the brief's numbers rule each one out:
- servos_12v costs $68 against $40 left, and the arm has torque to spare (1.18 of 1.62 N·m with sugar).
- prismatic reaches only 54 mm.
- long_slide reaches only 88 mm, and its rack lifts 1.1–3.6 mm against a 0.5 mm limit, which would also break apple, gelatin, tomato soup can and tennis ball.
- parallelogram raises the tip 61 mm at 85 mm.

That leaves pads.

- **Proposal 2** is a $0 probe of the one bridge between the current body and b000 that hasn't been tried: 45° with reach 11. If banana still fails at t = 0.02 s, the record shows that only the flat-pad angle decides banana against the wide boxes.
- **Proposal 3** records the part that would remove that conflict: a convex rocker pad. It uses only bench items: $0, about 23 machine minutes.

Nothing needs buying for proposals 1 and 2.

proposals.principle: A fingertip on a swinging joint rises by about R(1−cos q), and its face turns by q. For a given opening w ≈ R·sin q, a longer radius R needs a smaller q, so both the tip rise (about w²/2R) and the face tilt fall. reach_mm lengthens R (81 mm hinge-to-tip plus the reach).
proposals.hypothesis: Reach is the only pads parameter that has gained without loss: 7→11 mm gained a task and 11→17 mm gained tuna_fish_can (85 mm wide, 34 tall), held at a face tilt of +26° and a tip rise of +20 mm. Going from 17 to 30 mm makes R 98→111 mm (+13%). My estimate is that the 90–92 mm openings then need about 0.92–0.95 rad instead of 1.0, giving a face about 25–27° off and a tip about 19–21 mm high, which is tuna's working geometry. Pudding (38 tall) and sugar (45 tall) have more height than tuna's 34 mm, so the moving tip should get below their top edges. Sugar's arm load is 0.41+0.15×5.14 = 1.18 of 1.62 N·m, so torque is fine. At 57 mm the potted meat can needs a smaller q, so the pad's top leans in less over its top edge. Cheaper moves are exhausted: raising the pad angle above 28° always loses banana, and the catalogue swaps fail on the brief's own numbers (parallelogram tip +70 mm at 85 mm; long slide opens to only 86 mm with rack lift up to 3.9 mm against the 0.5 mm skip limit; 12 V costs $68 against $40 left). risks: dice / large_marker / wood_block_cube: longer, inward-tilted pads near the closed jaw (-0.17 rad) could collide or get the change refused for interference. At 17–26 mm the face tilt changes by only about 1°, so the grasp itself should survive.

iterations.notes:
I'm proposing two small pad changes and one untested design idea. I can't confidently predict any gains; they mainly test how close the failing tasks are to passing.

**What the record rules out:**
- **Mustard bottle (96 mm across):** the stock hinged jaw is the only part in the catalogue that opens past 88 mm. The parallelogram tops out at 88 mm, the long slide at 85 mm (and its rack lifts off the gear), and the short slide at 50 mm.
- **Faster servos:** the 12 V swap costs $68 against $40 left, and torque isn't what's failing anyway (the arm needs 1.06 of its 1.62 N*m for the mustard bottle).
- **Pad angle:** at least 34 deg loses banana, and even the 45 deg bodies didn't gain mustard or potted meat.
- **Reach:**
  - Below 17 mm loses pudding_box: the moving jaw lands on its top face.
  - At 24 mm or more, apple, tomato soup can and tennis ball are lost to a pad pressing on their tops.
  - The pudding_box failure comes from the moving fingertip rising at wide openings. The potted meat can fails with a pad on its rim, but I can't tell which pad that is from the report.

**Proposals:**
1. **Thicker TPU skin, 2 → 3 mm (aimed at mustard).** The only untried pad setting that changes the geometry at wide openings without moving angle or reach. For the same object width the jaw opens about 0.02 rad less, which by my estimate cuts about 1.7 mm of fingertip rise and 1.2 deg of tilt at 96 mm. That's small, but mustard already scores 0.5 and rises 16 mm before slipping. The groups most at risk are banana and the narrow objects.
2. **Thicker TPU skin plus reach 15.5 mm (aimed at potted meat).** The shorter reach should give more clearance over the 84 mm can. The thicker skin should cancel the extra 1.5 mm of fingertip rise that made reach 15.5 lose pudding_box. If my estimate is short, pudding_box (and possibly sugar box and tuna can) are lost again.
3. **Idea, not tested: separate reach for each pad.** Keep the moving pad at 17 mm and shorten the fixed pad to about 11 mm. It costs nothing to make (2 g PLA, 1 g TPU, 4 screws on hand). Whether it helps depends on which pad is pressing the can's rim, which only the simulator can tell us.

None of these needs anything bought; the two pad changes cost only print time.

proposals.hypothesis: This combines half steps from two held points. 32.5°/17 held all groups. 32.5°/15.5 lost pudding_box with the moving tip at +18 mm on a box 38 mm tall. Reach 16.25 recovers about 0.75 to 1 mm of clearance over the can, which misses only at the rim (2 mm). It costs pudding about 0.75 mm of moving-tip rise at 84 to 90 mm, which should fit inside the pudding margin seen between reaches 17 and 15.5. This is the only untried point in the reach bracket.

proposals.mechanism: mustard_bottle squeezed_down_out: at 95 mm the moving fingertip is +27 mm above the fixed one and its face is 31 to 53° off. It pushes the bottle down with N·sin(a) = 0.52 × 25 N ≈ 13 N, while friction on the fixed side gives only about 0.4 × 21 ≈ 8 N. The 431 g bottle rose 2 to 16 mm, then was pushed out downward.
proposals.principle: Two contacts hold only when their normals are opposed and horizontal. If the moving face can't be made parallel (that would need about a 60° pad angle against a 45° maximum, and no jaw in the catalogue opens to 96 mm), the downward component has to be carried by a support with an upward normal. A lip below the object on the fixed side gives that support, because the fixed fingertip, not the moving one, stays low (it does not rise with the opening).
proposals.hypothesis: The catalogue lip (1.5 mm) was refused only because the two pads overlapped near the fully closed jaw (−0.04 to 0.08 rad). This idea uses a 3 mm lip on the fixed pad only, a 2 mm relief chamfered into the bottom of the moving pad where that lip would meet it, and a printed close stop on the servo horn at about 0.12 rad (fingertips about 12 mm apart). The stop keeps the jaws out of the interference band, and it still closes past the smallest held object (the 17 mm dice, at 0.22 rad). The fixed fingertip sits a few mm above the table beside the bottle's lower curve. The hook catches under it and reacts the moving jaw's downward push, so the bottle is held by the fixed face and lip plus the moving face's squeeze.
risks: dice, large_marker, wood_block_cube: the close stop must stay below the 0.22 rad that the dice needs. 0.12 rad leaves 0.10 rad of margin.
flat_screwdriver, banana: these are low, lying objects, and the lip could catch the table or the object's underside as the jaw descends. That depends on System 1's clearance above the table.
pudding_box, sugar_box: no effect on the moving side. The fixed lip sits under the box, which only helps.

idea.name: fixed-side cradle lip with close stop
idea.description: Reprint the pads. The fixed pad gets a 3 mm inward hook along its bottom edge, angled up 10° so its upper surface acts as a ledge. The moving pad gets a 2 mm relief at its bottom inner corner so the hook has a pocket at the minimum opening. A small PLA stop tab screws to the jaw servo horn and meets the fixed jaw at 0.12 rad, so the pads never enter the −0.04 to 0.08 rad overlap that refused the catalogue lip. Wide lying objects that the tilted moving face pushes down (mustard) come to rest on the fixed-side ledge instead of sliding out under the fixed jaw.
idea.test: The simulator would need a pads builder with lip_mm applied to the fixed pad only, a relief pocket on the moving pad, and a minimum servo angle set by the stop (q_min = 0.12 rad). Then run mustard_bottle plus all held groups, and pass the interference check over 0.12 to 1.20 rad.

proposals.result: idea recorded, not tested: fixed-side cradle lip with close stop; it would need $0.00 from the manifest, 0 days, 28 machine min; within the budget left

iterations.notes:
What the record shows: no jaw in the catalogue can take the mustard bottle. It is 96 mm across. The parallelogram tops out at 88 mm, long_slide at 85 mm (and its rack skips at that width), and prismatic at 50 mm. They would also lose pudding (90 mm) and sugar (92 mm). servos_12v is refused on budget ($68 against $40 left), and torque isn't the problem anyway: 0.41 + 0.15×4.31 = 1.06 N·m against a 1.62 N·m stall. So mustard can only be fixed by changing the pads or by a new part.

On the hinge the moving face is about 31° off at 95 mm. Making it parallel would need a pad angle of about 60°, and the range stops at 45°. At 45° the opening also stops at 95 mm, which is less than 96. For mustard I therefore propose an idea, not a parameter change. It differs from the self-aligning ideas already recorded (flexure, rocker, variable-angle): it gives up making the faces antipodal and instead puts a support under the object on the fixed side.

Potted meat fails at the rim: the contact is at +40 to +42 mm with the top at +42. System 1's depth is only 6 to 13 mm. The one tested lever that lowers the moving fingertip at 55 to 70 mm openings is the pad angle (+2 mm at 31° vs −5 mm at 45° for a 55 mm opening). Pad angle is bracketed by banana: 32.5° held everything, 34° lost banana. Reach is bracketed by pudding: 17 mm holds it, 15.5 mm lost it. Proposals 1 and 2 make the last small steps inside these brackets. I'm only moderately confident in them: the miss looks like 1 to 3 mm, and each step buys about 1 mm.

proposals.principle: A finger can hold a side only if it passes beside the object and reaches below the top. Otherwise it presses on the top face. Thinner faces leave more free gap at the same servo opening.
proposals.hypothesis: Past trials treated the rim strike as a height problem, but reach 15.5, 14 and 11 did not produce a kept potted meat gain. This trial tests the lateral explanation instead. Taking TPU from 2 to 1.25 mm thins each face from 5 to 4.25 mm, which adds 1.5 mm of free gap. System 1's best side clearances were only 0.6 and 4.7 mm, so that is a meaningful share of the margin. The only TPU change on this body in the record, 2 to 3 mm, lost pudding_box and sugar_box with a pad on the top face, which fits the same explanation. The original prediction for that change, less tip rise from less servo angle, was wrong. Thinner has not been tried on this body. Cheaper moves are spent: reach is bracketed and pad angle is capped by banana. A jaw swap cannot be kept because the slides reach 85 mm and the parallelogram 88 mm, against pudding_box at 90 mm and sugar_box at 92 mm. Confidence is low, but the result separates lateral from vertical clearance either way.
risks: pudding_box and sugar_box: 1.5 mm more separation needs about 0.02 rad more servo angle (0.013 rad/mm at 85-95 mm), or about 1.3 mm more tip rise and 1 deg more tilt. Pudding is near its limit, since reach 15.5 lost it, but the 2 to 3 mm result suggests thinner may help rather than hurt.
tuna_fish_can: 85 mm wide and only 34 mm tall, so it is sensitive to the same 1.3 mm of tip rise.
flat_screwdriver: it is sensitive to fixed-jaw alignment, since reach 14 lost it to fixed_jaw_missed, and thinner faces shift the contact plane by 0.75 mm.
Friction is assumed to stay 0.9 at 1.25 mm of TPU. If it does not, the heavy objects sugar_box and tomato_soup_can are at risk.

proposals.principle: A contact tilted by a pushes the object with N sin(a), and friction mu N must hold that plus the weight. The contact patch's spread along the object also resists it pitching out of the grip.
proposals.hypothesis: The reg numbers show a marginal failure. The demand is 25 x sin 31 = 12.9 N plus 4.2 N of weight, or 17.1 N. Pad angle 32.5, which already held all 19 groups at reach 17, removes 1.5 deg, or about 0.6 N. It did not gain mustard alone, so this adds width 24, a value not tried in the visible record. Width does not change the Coulomb budget, so it cannot remove the tilt. It can double the lever against pitching on a 191 mm long bottle gripped by a 12 mm pad, which may be what turns a marginal grip into slip. This is a bet on that secondary effect. It is cheap, needing only a slightly larger print and no purchases. No catalogue jaw reaches 96 mm: the slides stop at 85 mm and the parallelogram at 88 mm. Only the revolute jaw can stay.
risks: banana: the most angle-sensitive group. It held at 32.5 deg but was lost at 33.25 and 34 deg to a side press. A wider pad on its curved side could add a new contact, so this is the most likely loss.
racquetball: it was lost at 32.5 deg with reach 16.25 by squeezed_down_out, so it has little margin at this angle, though reach stays at 17 here.
flat_screwdriver: a 24 mm pad may catch the uneven handle differently from a 12 mm pad.
dice and large_marker: these should survive, because the wider pad does not change the closing geometry, but the added wrist mass is untested.

proposals.principle: Tilt and tip rise both grow with servo angle. A longer radius reaches the same opening at a smaller angle, which reduces both.
proposals.hypothesis: Reach 17 to 19 raises the radius about 2%, which adds about 1.9 mm of separation at a fixed servo angle. At about 77 mm/rad near 95 mm, that saves about 0.025 rad, or 1.4 deg of tilt and about 1.7 mm of tip rise. With pad angle 32.5 the tilt becomes about 28 deg. The push falls from 12.9 to about 11.7 N, so demand is about 15.9 N against the 18.4 N capacity, a margin of about 16% instead of about 7%. That is my best estimate for reg_mustard_bottle. rva000 is harder, with its contact pushing 53 deg down, so the group may still fail there. Reach 19 is untried and sits between 17, which holds apple, and 21, where apple was lost at 34 deg. Pad angle alone cannot deliver this, because banana caps it near 32.5 deg. banana: held at 32.5 deg with reach 17 but sensitive above that. The extra reach also shifts its contact slightly.
racquetball: it was lost at 32.5 deg with reach 16.25, which shows this neighbourhood is noisy, so it could drop again even though the reach change goes the other way.
cup and other tall objects: a longer pad brings the tips closer to their tops on approach, though they are all shorter than apple.

proposals.principle: A tilted contact pushes the object with N sin(a), which friction must hold. Fingertip rise on a swinging joint grows as R(1 - cos q), so any reduction in the closing angle q at 96 mm cuts both the tilt and the rise.
proposals.hypothesis: Use pad angle 32.5 deg with TPU 0.8 mm (two 0.4 mm perimeters), keeping reach 17 and width 12. Demand is about 25 x sin 31 = 12.9 N plus 4.2 N of weight, or 17.1 N, and the reg placement rose 16 mm before slipping, so it is marginal. Both changes have held all 19 groups separately: 32.5/17 at TPU 2, and 31/17 at TPU 1.25. The combination is untried. The evidence on TPU is weak but points one way: at 31 deg, reach 15.5, TPU 3 closed at 1.04 rad with the tip at +24 mm, while TPU 2 closed at 0.97 rad with the tip at +20 mm. Both were failed pudding grasps, so this is not a clean measurement, and face geometry alone could give the opposite sign. This trial tests that sign. The brief quotes friction 0.9 for the TPU skin, and I assume it stays 0.9 at 0.8 mm. Cheaper moves are exhausted: pad angle above 32.5 loses banana (33.25 and 34 both did), and reach 19 only turned the mustard failure into moving_jaw_on_top_face. No catalogue swap can hold this object: the slides reach at most 85 mm and the parallelogram 88 mm, against 96 mm needed. servos_12v is refused at $68 against $40 left, and it would not address this anyway, since the holding torque of about 1.06 N*m at 431 g is under the 1.62 N*m stall. Nothing needs buying; the pads use on-hand screws and a small print within the 522 machine minutes.

pudding_box and sugar_box: these are the most sensitive to tip rise at 90 to 92 mm. They should survive if q falls, but would be at risk if the sign is the opposite, as they were at TPU 3.
racquetball: it was lost at 32.5/16.25 by squeezed_down_out, so it is sensitive around this angle. Reach stays at 17 here, which held it.

proposals.mechanism: force_limit: a pad presses down on the potted meat can's rim (28 N at +42 mm and 53 N at +40 mm, top at +42). Secondary target: squeezed_down_out on mustard_bottle.
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel to the fixed face at one opening only. A tilted face also narrows the gap towards the hinge, so a tall flat-sided object meets the pad at its rim. Moving that parallel opening to the object's width removes the tilt there, and a smaller tilt also reduces the N sin(a) push on wide objects.
proposals.hypothesis: Set pad angle 35.5 deg, width 24 mm, reach 17 mm. The brief gives about 0.61 to 0.62 rad (about 35 deg) of servo at 57 mm, so a 35.5 deg pad should be nearly parallel at the can's width. The current 31 deg pad is about 4 to 5 deg off, bottom swung out, by the same estimate. This is an inference, not a measured rim clearance, and the visible record shows no potted meat gain at 33.25 deg, so the rim theory is unproven. At 96 mm the mustard tilt should fall from 31 deg to about 26 deg. Using the reg numbers with a 25 N moving contact, demand falls from 17.1 N to about 15 N against 18.4 N of friction capacity. The wider pad is the untested part: banana was lost at 33.25 and 34 deg with 12 mm pads, including fixed_jaw_missed at 39 mm on its curved body, and a 24 mm pad may keep contact there. Cheaper moves are used up: reach 11 to 19, TPU 0.8 to 3 and angle 32.5 at 12 or 24 mm gained nothing or lost a group. The swaps cannot help: the catalogue jaws top out at 85 to 88 mm, below sugar_box (92 mm) and mustard_bottle (96 mm). servos_12v is refused at $68 against $40 left, and it addresses no failing mechanism: the arm needs about 1.06 N*m for 431 g against a 1.62 N*m stall. This is a reprint of the same pads and needs no purchase.

dice, large_marker, wood_block_cube: the moving face tilts further with its bottom swung in at small widths, about 22 deg at 17 mm. The 34 deg trials are not recorded as losing them, but that record does not cover 35.5 deg.
pudding_box, sugar_box, tuna_fish_can: these should improve because the face is more parallel, but q at a given opening rises slightly above about 31 deg, which adds tip rise.
racquetball, plum, lemon: rolling objects near 53 to 59 mm change their contact angle, though it moves towards parallel.

proposals.principle: A contact tilted by a pushes the object out with N sin(a), and friction mu N must hold that push plus the weight. Reducing the tilt at 96 mm reduces the demand directly.
proposals.hypothesis: Set pad angle 34 deg, width 24 mm, reach 17 mm. This is the most conservative step that still changes the wide-opening tilt. The tilt at 96 mm falls from 31 deg to about 28 deg, so demand falls from 17.1 N to about 15.9 N against 18.4 N of capacity. That gives about 2.5 N of margin instead of 1.3 N for lift acceleration on the marginal reg placement. Width 24 held every group at 32.5 deg, and 34 deg with 12 mm pads lost only banana, by a 5 to 13 N side press at about t=3.6 s. The visible record has no trial of 34 deg with 24 mm, so this tests that pairing directly. The weak point is rva000_mustard_bottle, which stuck with a 53 deg contact on the curved surface at +11 mm. A 3 deg change may not fix that placement, and the group needs both placements, so confidence is low. The gain is predicted because the mechanism points that way, not because the margin is comfortable.
risks: banana: lost at 34 deg with 12 mm pads to a side press. A wider pad might keep the fixed jaw on the curved body, or might press its side sooner.

pudding_box, sugar_box: these sit close to moving_jaw_on_top_face, and the width 24 trial showed that mechanism among its failures. Which group it hit is not stated. The held result at 32.5 deg with 24 mm suggests they survive.
Small objects (dice, large_marker): the bottom swings in further, but angles up to 34 deg are not recorded as losing them.

proposals.mechanism: squeezed_down_out on mustard_bottle, attacked through both tilt and servo angle at the 96 mm opening.
proposals.principle: A longer radius from the hinge opens the fingertips further per radian, so the same width is reached at a smaller servo angle, with less tilt and less tip rise (R(1 - cos q)). A larger pad angle removes more tilt on top of that.
proposals.hypothesis: Set pad angle 34 deg, width 24 mm, reach 19 mm. Reach 19 at 32.5 deg saved an estimated 0.025 rad at 96 mm, about 1.4 deg of tilt and 1.7 mm of tip rise. That trial no longer listed squeezed_down_out among its failures, but it showed moving_jaw_on_top_face instead. The added angle lowers the moving tip at the same opening, which should counter that new failure. Estimated tilt is about 26.5 deg, for a demand of about 15.4 N against 18.4 N, and this is the largest margin of the three proposals at the known-tested angle. It is the only proposal that changes reach, so it shows whether the on-top failure at reach 19 can be cured with angle. Potted meat is not expected to gain, because a longer pad does nothing for rim clearance.
risks: banana: same angle risk as the 34 deg proposal, and reach 19 has not been tried at this angle.
pudding_box, sugar_box, tuna_fish_can: a longer hand changes their clearance over low objects. Reach 19 was not recorded as losing them at 32.5 deg, and the larger angle should help further.
dice, wood_block_cube: longer tips swing further when nearly closed. The clearance to the table should still be set by System 1's depth search.

iterations.notes: This is the last iteration, and all three proposals are low-confidence, free reprints of the current pads. They use only printed material and need no purchase. The tilt, angle and force figures are my estimates from the brief's table and the reg placement's contact forces, not simulator readings. Banana is the main threat to all three. No swap is proposed: the catalogue jaws top out at 85 to 88 mm, below sugar_box (92 mm) and mustard_bottle (96 mm), and servos_12v is unaffordable at $68 against $40 and addresses no failing mechanism. No new idea is recorded, because the ones most relevant to these failures (self-aligning pad, variable-angle pad, split-reach pads) are already on file. If these trials fail, 19/21 is probably near the limit of this hinged jaw within the pads' 0 to 45 deg range, and the self-aligning or variable-angle moving pad would be the next thing to build.
